data.summary: The pi-web directory is a declarative scenario-definition bundle for the optional "pi Web UI" scenario inside the app (AIO) stack. It pairs a TOML scenario descriptor (id, installer, always_on flag) with a Dockerfile fragment that documents how the pi-web npm package is provisioned and exposed. Together they tell the platform manager how to optionally install and surface a Next.js-based pi browser UI via the app container's entrypoint on port 30141.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: A comment-only Dockerfile fragment that documents the pi-web scenario: npm global install of pi-web into /usr/local/bin, auto-launch from app/entrypoint.sh on 0.0.0.0:30141, and iframe embedding rationale.
file_insights.source_summary: The source is entirely comment lines prefixed with '#', describing the scenario: pi local browser UI (agegr/pi-web, Next.js), npm global install to /usr/local/bin/pi-web, service launched by app/entrypoint.sh on 0.0.0.0:30141 with auto-restart and logs at ~/.aio/pi-web.log, panel button declared as type=web iframe in app/services.toml, and compose publishing port 30141 directly to the app container because sub-path proxying is impossible.
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment contains no executable build instructions; it is a documentation/annotation block consumed by the scenario build pipeline as the L4 ("pi-web") layer description. It records the design decision to skip an L5 compose service and instead install the pi-web npm package globally into the app container, with the app entrypoint auto-starting the service and the panel embedding it through a type=web iframe. It also explains why caddy sub-path proxying is not usable for pi-web (Next.js absolute /_next/ asset references and built-in /api/* routes).
responsibilities: Document the pi-web scenario build layer and its rationale
Record the npm-global install location and launch contract (/usr/local/bin/pi-web, 0.0.0.0:30141)
Explain why the UI is served on a direct published port rather than behind a caddy sub-path
Note entrypoint auto-start behavior, crash restart, and log file location

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Scenario manifest declaring the pi-web scenario metadata (id, name, description, category=app, installer=npm, always_on=false) for the manager's service toggle wizard.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines keys: id="pi-web", name="pi Web UI", description (local browser UI for pi, @agegr/pi-web globally installed via npm to /usr/local/bin, requires node>=22.19, entrypoint auto-starts port 30141, panel iframe embedded, app publishes the port), category="app", installer="npm", always_on=false. Inline comments capture the S1 (2026-09-10) change from always_on to an optional scenario and the .aio/enabled.toml opt-in behavior.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the machine-readable declaration of the pi Web UI scenario, consumed by the platform manager when rendering the creation wizard's service switches. It marks the scenario as optional (always_on = false) following the S1 decision that flipped it from always-on to an opt-in toggle named "pi Web", while noting the app entrypoint's `command -v pi-web` guard means absence of the package is handled gracefully (silent skip, iframe health-check failure hides the button). It specifies the npm installer and the runtime requirement of node >= 22.19.
responsibilities: Declare scenario identity and human-readable metadata for the manager wizard
Specify installer type (npm) and the pi Web service toggle default
Mark the scenario as optional (always_on = false) rather than part of the main stack
Document node version requirement and entrypoint/iframe behavior
